thread:
infra-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: high error rate and connection resets for private-linked workloads in Azure West US 3 (region id: westus3). alert_id=PD-5773

oncall-sre: acked — looking now. show me what the signals are.

Alex R: seeing massive BGP session resets to our customer on-prem peers across multiple VNets. error rate spikes at 01:44 UTC.

Mei C: confirmed — telemetry shows flapping BGP prefixes for our Private-NAT gateway and some ExpressRoute circuits. VPN tunnels show frequent IKE rekeys then drop.

Samir P: do we have any Azure status note? I can't find a clear service health entry for vwan/expressroute yet.

NetOps: Azure portal is reporting a "network control plane" incident in westus3 for routing/peering. Not full outage, but increased churn and route convergence issues. link: https://status.azure.com/ (customer-facing notice appears truncated)

Alex R: impact: customer apps using Private deployment in westus3 -> intermittent connection failures to on-prem services and Customer-managed DNS queries failing intermittently. Some internal health checks show 502s to private endpoints.

Liz CS: paging a couple of affected customers now (pre-emptive). I put a note in CS tracker: ticket 13244. We'll coordinate messaging.

oncall-sre: quick mitigation plan: 1) identify affected Dedicated pools/VNets 2) failover routes to secondary region (westus2) where feasible 3) advise customers to temporarily route critical traffic via Dedicated peering or fallback public endpoints 4) lift rate-limited retries at app layer to avoid amplification.

John D: adding routing detail — route tables show duplicate Next-Hops during the churn; some routes are oscillating between on-prem path and local internet breakouts. Likely route leak / rapid withdraws causing ECMP imbalance.

Mei C: snippets from control plane logs:
```
[01:43:12] BGP: neighbor 10.2.3.1 CLOSED (remote reset)
[01:43:13] BGP: Received UPDATE: withdraw 10.10.0.0/16
[01:43:14] BGP: ADD 10.10.0.0/16 via 10.4.1.5 metric 100
[01:43:15] BGP: neighbor 10.2.3.1 ESTABLISHED
```
This repeats rapidly across peers.

oncall-sre: can we programmatically mute noisy alerts and keep only high-severity ones? infra-bot might be spamming PD.

infra-bot: Alert dedupe in progress. Suppressing duplicate BGP-reset alerts for 10m window.

Samir P: mitigation step I executed: removed a problematic route advertisement from our westus3 virtual-appliance route reflector, forcing traffic to prefer westus2 via our geo-bgp preference. Early signs: decreased connection resets for a subset of customers.

Alex R: added a temporary Azure route table override for critical subnets to point to transit-gateway in westus2. This will route around local unstable path. Note: this may increase latency for some flows.

Mei C: rolling DNS mitigation: switching TTLs to 60s and updating private DNS zone records for the most impacted services to point to westus2 endpoints where available. Watchouts: some customers use locked down DNS/VPN that only allow westus3 addresses.

Liz CS: notifying affected customers: message draft ready — will call customers with open sessions. status: partial degraded connectivity, routing instability in westus3, mitigation in progress, recommend failover to westus2 or use public fallback.

NetOps: coordinating with Azure support & our ExpressRoute contacts. They've acknowledged region-level control plane instability and say they're throttling updates to reduce churn. No ETA yet.

Alex R: quick check: are any Dedicated pools fully offline? I see a couple of hosts reporting elevated tokenization latency but still accepting requests. No full host-level OOMs.

Mei C: Prometheus Grafana panels show token error spike: 5xxs up from 0.2% to 6.8% across the westus3 private cluster between 01:40-01:55 UTC. KV-cache hit rate unaffected.

oncall-sre: operational actions checklist (doing now):
- [x] Acknowledge pager
- [x] Quiet noisy PD alerts (infra-bot)
- [x] Identify impacted customers & mark in CS tracker
- [x] Apply temporary route preference to westus2 for critical subnets
- [x] Start DNS TTL reduction and update private records
- [ ] Prepare canary shift of 10% traffic to westus2 for low-latency customers
- [ ] Draft incident postmortem stub

Samir P: starting the canary shift for a single customer now (id: cust-217). rolling update triggered.

Alex R: logs from the first canary: connectivity stabilized for that customer after reroute. No application regressions seen in 10 minutes.

Mei C: caution — some customers report that on-prem firewalls dropped the new path due to asymmetric routing. We've flagged this to NetOps to coordinate with customers' network teams.

NetOps: I've opened a support escalation with Azure networking team, provided BGP dumps + timestamps, asked for route dampening knobs. They suggested they are applying internal dampening but won't give a public ETA.

Liz CS: customer update sent to the 6 impacted accounts. Two customers asked for immediate manual failover assistance — scheduling 1:1 calls.

oncall-sre: handoff note for next on-call at 02:00 UTC:
- Current status: control plane instability in westus3 causing BGP/VPN churn. Partial mitigations applied: route preference to westus2 for critical subnets, DNS updates in progress, canary shifts showing success.
- Outstanding: Azure ETA unknown, some customers with strict on-prem firewall rules may need manual network changes, continue canary and expand to 20% if stable.
- Monitoring: watch BGP session state, 5xx rate on private endpoints, and PD alert dedupe.

Samir P: taking over oncall at 02:00 UTC. I'll watch the canary expansion and coordinate with NetOps for customer network reachability.

infra-bot: Incident channel pinned: incident/1850001234. Automated timeline started.

Mei C: reminder to attach BGP dumps and route diagnostics to the incident page. logs: s3://redwood-ops/incident-1850001234/bgp-dumps/

John D: quick note — if Azure confirms control-plane fix, we should cautiously remove temp route overrides after 30-60 minutes of stability to avoid oscillation.

oncall-sre: thanks all. I'll close out the active paging after secure handoff. Keep posting updates in this thread; include any customer-impacting changes. :thumbsup:

Liz CS: will keep CS updates rolling and collect any customer-side debug info.

Samir P: ack. starting expanded canary to 20% now.

(02:40 UTC) NetOps: Azure triage says they're seeing clear reduction in control-plane churn; asking us to confirm if withdrawal storm subsided. Please report BGP stability.

Mei C: BGP resets down to baseline for our monitored peers over the past 10m. 5xx rates trending down to ~0.8%. Looks like mitigations + Azure dampening helped.

infra-bot: Auto-close suggestion: no. Incident remains active until all temp routes rolled back and customers confirmed.

Samir P: will prepare rollback playbook once we get sustained 45m of stability and coordinate with CS for final customer confirmations.

oncall-sre: closing active pager now, incident remains in active monitoring. Handoff complete.

-- end of thread --
